This utility simulates a client generating **traces**, **metrics**, **logs**, **profiles**, and Splunk AlwaysOn Profiling data as OTLP logs. It is useful for testing and demonstration purposes.

## Installing

To install the latest version run the following command:

```console
go install github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/cmd/telemetrygen@latest
```

Check the [`go install` reference](https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-install) to install specific versions.

### Docker build

You can build locally the Docker image with:

```bash
make docker-telemetrygen
```

Using github actions, we also push a docker image on commit to main or on release to this [Github docker registry](https://github.com/orgs/open-telemetry/packages/container/package/opentelemetry-collector-contrib%2Ftelemetrygen).

## Running

First, you'll need an OpenTelemetry Collector to receive the telemetry data. Follow the project's instructions for a detailed setting up guide. The following configuration file should be sufficient:

config.yaml:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317

exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug]
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug]
    profiles:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug]
```

Profiles support is experimental. Enable it in the Collector with `--feature-gates=+service.profilesSupport`.

Starting OpenTelemetry collector via docker:
```
docker run -p 4317:4317 -v $(pwd)/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol-contrib/config.yaml ghcr.io/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.149.0
```

Other options for running the collector are documented here https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/getting-started/

## Export timeout

The maximum time to wait for signals to reach the destination can be configured with the following flag:

```console
--timeout=10s #Defaults to 10s
```

## Batching signals

All telemetry signals have batching capability configurable with the following flags:

```console
--batch=false #Defaults to true, no flag needed for batching
```

```console
--batch-size=1000 #Defaults to 100
```

Once the OpenTelemetry Collector instance is up and running, run `telemetrygen` for your desired telemetry:

### Traces

```console
telemetrygen traces --otlp-insecure --duration 5s
```

Or, to generate a specific number of traces:

```console
telemetrygen traces --otlp-insecure --traces 1
```

Or, to generate traces continuously (use `--duration inf` with `--rate` for throttling):

```console
telemetrygen traces --otlp-insecure --duration inf --rate 0.1
```

To send traces in secure connection, see [examples/secure-tracing](../../examples/secure-tracing/)

Check `telemetrygen traces --help` for all the options.

### Logs

```console
telemetrygen logs --otlp-insecure --duration 5s
```

Or, to generate a specific number of logs:

```console
telemetrygen logs --otlp-insecure --logs 1
```

Or, to generate logs continuously:

```console
telemetrygen logs --otlp-insecure --duration inf --rate 0.1
```

To send logs in secure connection, see [examples/secure-tracing](../../examples/secure-tracing/)

Check `telemetrygen logs --help` for all the options.

### Splunk AlwaysOn Profiling logs

The `profiling` command generates synthetic CPU and allocation profiles in the same OTLP log format used by the Splunk Java profiler. Profile bodies contain base64-encoded, gzip-compressed pprof data. Profiling is disabled by default, matching the instrumentation libraries.

```console
SPLUNK_PROFILER_ENABLED=true \
SPLUNK_PROFILER_MEMORY_ENABLED=true \
SPLUNK_PROFILER_LOGS_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318/v1/logs \
telemetrygen profiling --duration inf --rate 1 --workers 1 \
  --samples 100 --stack-depth 32 --unique-stacks 20 --batch-size 100
```

`SPLUNK_PROFILER_ENABLED=true` enables CPU profile records. `SPLUNK_PROFILER_MEMORY_ENABLED=true` additionally enables allocation profile records. The memory setting has no effect when CPU profiling is disabled, as with the Java instrumentation. The logs endpoint defaults to `http://localhost:4318/v1/logs`; set `SPLUNK_PROFILER_LOGS_ENDPOINT` to change it. Use `--otlp-insecure` for an unencrypted local Collector endpoint if needed.

`--rate` is profile log records per second **per worker**. With both CPU and memory profiling enabled, generated records alternate between CPU and allocation profiles. `--profiles` sets a finite number of log records per worker and is ignored when `--duration` is set. `--batch-size` controls the maximum number of records sent in one OTLP request (default 100); smaller rates automatically use smaller batches to keep export latency low. Encoded pprof bodies are reused within each batch to reduce CPU spent on repeated compression. `--samples`, `--stack-depth`, and `--unique-stacks` control the generated profile shape. The generator emits synthetic pprof data; it does not run a JVM or sample real application stacks.

Use `--errors` to make a percentage of profile log records carry intentionally invalid pprof payloads. For example, `--rate 100 --errors 10` generates 10 invalid records for every 100 generated records (with `--errors` kept between 0 and 100). Invalid records retain the profiling attributes, use error severity, and rotate through malformed base64, invalid gzip, and invalid pprof content so they exercise payload conversion failures while remaining valid OTLP log records.

The command also exports these cumulative metrics to the OTLP metrics endpoint on the same collector, every 5 minutes by default. Use `--interval` to change the reporting interval:

| Metric | Attributes | Meaning |
| ------ | ---------- | ------- |
| `telemetrygen.profiling.log_records` | `status=sent\|rejected\|failed` | Number of acknowledged profile log records, records explicitly rejected in an OTLP partial-success response, or records in a failed request. Failed records were not acknowledged and may have an uncertain delivery outcome if the connection failed after the collector received them. |
| `telemetrygen.profiling.export_errors` | `error.type=busy\|network\|rejected\|other` | Number of failed or partially rejected log export requests by error category. |

For a Splunk Observability Cloud chart, select `telemetrygen.profiling.log_records`, group or split by `status`, and chart the `sent`, `rejected`, and `failed` time series. Add a second chart for `telemetrygen.profiling.export_errors` and split by `error.type` to see busy, network, rejected, and other errors. The counters are cumulative for the process lifetime. The collector must have a metrics receiver and metrics pipeline configured for the OTLP endpoint; metrics export errors are logged by telemetrygen.

Build from this module with `go build -o telemetrygen .`.

### Metrics

```console
telemetrygen metrics --otlp-insecure --duration 5s
```

Or, to generate a specific number of metrics:

```console
telemetrygen metrics --otlp-insecure --metrics 1
```

Or, to generate metrics continuously:

```console
telemetrygen metrics --otlp-insecure --duration inf --rate 0.1
```

To send metrics in secure connection, see [examples/secure-tracing](../../examples/secure-tracing/)

Check `telemetrygen metrics --help` for all the options.

### Profiles

Generate profiles over OTLP/gRPC:

```console
telemetrygen profiles --otlp-insecure --profiles 10
```

The profile payload can be shaped with `--samples`, `--stack-depth`, and `--unique-stacks`. Use `--size` to add string data to each profile, `--rate` or `--duration` to control the load, and `--batch` with `--batch-size` to send multiple profiles in one request. Use `--invalid-profiles` to include that many invalid profiles in each export request. Each worker randomly shuffles the invalidation fields and cycles through invalid sample type and period indices, profile and sample attribute references, stack and link references, and invalid sample value shapes before repeating. The default maximum gRPC request size is 4 MiB; change it with `--max-message-mib` when sending larger batches.

The command sends OTLP metrics describing the run at startup and every five minutes by default: `telemetrygen_profiles_workers`, `telemetrygen_profiles_rate` (per worker), `telemetrygen_profiles_batch_enabled`, `telemetrygen_profiles_batch_size` (configured value), `telemetrygen_profiles_effective_batch_size` (profiles per request; 1 when batching is disabled), and `telemetrygen_profiles_invalid_profiles` (invalid profiles per request). Set `--interval` to change the reporting interval. The configured OTLP endpoint must accept metrics as well as profiles.

For example, to put five invalid profiles in every batch of 30:

```console
telemetrygen profiles --otlp-insecure --duration inf --rate 1 \
  --batch --batch-size 30 --invalid-profiles 5
```

```console
telemetrygen profiles --otlp-insecure --duration 5m --rate 10 \
  --samples 1000 --stack-depth 64 --unique-stacks 100 \
  --batch --batch-size 10
```

Check `telemetrygen profiles --help` for all the options.

## Attributes

Custom attributes can be added at two different levels, using two different flags:

| Flag | Sets | Applied to |
| ---- | ---- | ---------- |
| `--otlp-attributes` | Resource attributes | The OTLP resource, once per run. They describe the entity producing the telemetry and are shared by every span, metric data point, log record, and profile. |
| `--telemetry-attributes` | Span, metric data point, log record, or profile attributes | Each generated telemetry item individually. |

Because `service.name` is a resource attribute, `--otlp-attributes service.name="my-service"` overrides the `--service` flag.

Both flags accept the same value formats: `key="value"`, `key=true`, `key=false`, `key=<integer>`, and `key=["value1", "value2", ...]` for slices. All items of a slice must have the same type. Both flags may be repeated to set multiple attributes.

String values must keep their double quotes when they reach `telemetrygen`, so escape them (or wrap the whole argument in single quotes) to prevent the shell from removing them:

```console
telemetrygen traces --otlp-insecure --traces 1 \
  --otlp-attributes service.name=\"my-service\" \
  --otlp-attributes host.name=\"host-1\" \
  --telemetry-attributes http.request.method=\"GET\" \
  --telemetry-attributes http.response.status_code=200
```

This generates a resource carrying `service.name` and `host.name`, and spans that each carry `http.request.method` and `http.response.status_code`.
